chapter: Hopkins, Kelly's Stables and Red Allen
title: Pedal vibraphones and the band within a band at Edgar Hayes
summary: When dampers came in around 1936-37 he played vibes choruses and recorded for Decca with Edgar Hayes in a quartet with Rudy Powell.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: So then they introduced the vibraphones with the damper. You know, a pedal where you could stop the vibrations.
Yeah.
So then I started to try to play little choruses, courses, you know.
Yeah. When was that, what year?
Well, this was around '36, '37.
Oh, that --
Well, we recorded. I recorded with Edgar Hayes on Decca.
Yeah.
Quite a few records on vibraphones, you know.
Oh.
With Bill Barnell singing sometimes. And Bob Stevens, he loved the vibraphones, so we had sort of a quartet, with Rudy Powell, clarinet; bass, guitar, piano and myself.
Like a band within a band, you mean?
Yeah, a band within a band.
Yeah. Oh, so that was nice.
So I would play the vibraphones sometimes.
Yeah.
Some tunes we didn't even use drums at all.
Yes.
Just the bass and the guitar.
Yeah. Fancy that.
Kept the rhythm going and I played the vibes, along with Rudy Powell. We would play in harmony, things, you know.
Yeah. Rudy was in that band that kept rehearsing all the time.
Yeah. Well, he lived right next door.
(Laughter)
Yeah.
He lived next door to the Renaissance Casino.
(Laughter)
